papers.title: Convexity is overrated: Shortest paths on 4-polytopes are hard to compute
papers.abstract: We prove that computing geodesic distance on the boundary of a rational convex $4$-polytope is NP-hard. We then construct rational $4$-polytopes with two rational points joined by exponentially many shortest paths of equal rational length, disproving several conjectures along the way. For the same problem, we also prove SQRTSUM-hardness under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. By a separate argument, we show that the square of the geodesic distance between distinct rational boundary points of a rational convex polytope is a totally positive multiquadratic number.

papers.title: Subexponential Algorithms for Continuous Euclidean $k$-Means in Subpolylogarithmic Dimension
papers.abstract: Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{Q}^d$ and an integer $k$, the continuous Euclidean $k$-means problem asks for $k$ centers in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that minimize the sum of squared distances from the input points to their nearest centers. In one dimension, the problem can be solved in polynomial time by dynamic programming. In higher dimensions, the algorithm of Inaba, Katoh, and Imai [SoCG 1994] runs in polynomial time when both $k$ and $d$ are fixed. Mahajan, Nimbhorkar, and Varadarajan [TCS 2012] showed that the problem is NP-hard even in the plane when $k$ is part of the input, answering a question of Dasgupta [2008]. In this paper, we give a deterministic exact algorithm for continuous Euclidean $k$-means. For arbitrary $k$ and $d=(\log n)^{o(1)}$, the algorithm runs in $O^*(2^{o(n)})$ time and uses polynomial space. Aman, Karthik C. S., and Punna [ESA 2024] asked whether the $2^n$ time bound for Euclidean $k$-means can be improved in high dimensions. Our result gives an affirmative answer to the corresponding question in subpolylogarithmic dimension.

papers.title: Polylogarithmic Approximation for Packing Convex Polyhedra
papers.abstract: We study translational packing of convex polyhedra in three dimensions. Given $n$ convex polyhedra in $\mathbb{R}^3$, we seek a placement with pairwise disjoint interiors that minimizes the volume of an axis-parallel bounding box. Constant-factor approximation algorithms are known when rotations are allowed, but no approximation guarantee was previously known for arbitrary convex polyhedra with fixed orientations. A central difficulty is that, unlike in the plane, the total volume and the coordinate extents of the objects do not provide a useful lower bound on the optimum: even objects with small total volume and small diameter may require a container of large volume. We overcome this difficulty using a better geometric lower bound based on a surprising connection to Wang and Zahl's celebrated recent proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture. Using this, we obtain a polynomial-time $n^{o(1)}$-approximation algorithm. A recent strengthening of Wang and Zahl's theorem claimed by OpenAI gives a polylogarithmic approximation ratio for the same algorithm. Our ideas extend to bin and strip packing: for any fixed $\delta>0$, we obtain the same approximation guarantees for translational packing of convex polyhedra whose coordinate widths are at most a $1-\delta$ fraction of the corresponding container widths.

papers.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $\Delta^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[ c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}. \] The second equality confirms a conjecture of Bukh, Matou\v{s}ek, and Nivasch, who established the upper bound. The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions of the author.

papers.title: Persistent Stiefel-Whitney Classes of Tangent Bundles
papers.abstract: Stiefel--Whitney classes are invariants of the tangent bundle of a smooth manifold, represented as cohomology classes of the base manifold. These classes are essential in obstruction theory, embedding problems, and cobordism theory. In this work, we propose a concrete algorithm to compute persistent cohomology classes representing these characteristic classes. Given a point cloud, we construct a \v{C}ech or alpha filtration and apply the Wu formula using the cup product and Steenrod squares. The algorithm runs in polynomial time in the number of simplices without estimating tangent spaces or constructing a classifying map. Under suitable hypotheses on the filtration, the resulting classes represent those of a closed smooth manifold even when the filtration contains additional wedge summands on whose reduced cohomology all positive Steenrod squares vanish. For sufficiently large samples drawn independently and uniformly from the manifold, recovery holds with high probability over an interval of scales. We present experiments on triangulated four-manifolds and on point clouds from image patches and a molecular conformation space.

papers.title: The sublevel Flood bifiltration: towards scalable 2-parameter persistent homology
papers.abstract: Multiparameter persistent homology is a rapidly developing branch of topological data analysis that improves the robustness of single-parameter persistent homology to outliers, while still capturing the metric characteristics of the data. However, a notable limitation is its lack of scalability. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach for efficiently computing 2-parameter persistent homology on large point sets. Our work extends the Flood filtration, originally developed for single-parameter persistence. Our construction, called the sublevel Flood bifiltration, offers a scalable approximation of the sublevel offset bifiltration. We show that it benefits from theoretical stability properties and describe how to compute it efficiently. We demonstrate the performance of our approach in classification tasks on low-dimensional synthetic datasets, where density awareness is critical, as well as on real-world time series datasets.

papers.title: MergeDJD: A Fast Constructive Algorithm with Piece Merging for the Two-Dimensional Irregular Bin Packing Problem
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional irregular bin packing problem (2DIBPP) aims to pack a given set of irregular polygons, referred to as pieces, into fixed-size rectangular bins without overlap, while maximizing bin utilization. Although numerous metaheuristic algorithms have been proposed for the 2DIBPP, many industrial applications favor simpler constructive heuristics due to their deterministic behavior and low computational overhead. Among such methods, the DJD algorithm proposed by L'opez-Camacho et al. is one of the most competitive constructive heuristics for the 2DIBPP. However, DJD is less effective for cutting instances, in which many pieces can be seamlessly combined into larger polygons. To address the issue, we propose MergeDJD, a novel constructive algorithm that integrates and extends the DJD framework. MergeDJD first preprocesses the instance by iteratively identifying groups of pieces that can be combined into larger and more regular piece. It then employs an improved version of DJD, in which the placement strategy is enhanced to better handle non-convex and combined shapes, to pack all resulting pieces into bins. Computational experiments on 1,089 well-known benchmark instances show that MergeDJD consistently outperforms DJD on 1,083 instances while maintaining short runtimes. Notably, MergeDJD attains new best known values on 515 instances. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the proposed components. To facilitate reproducibility and future research, we have open-sourced the complete implementation and provided interfaces for visualizing packing results.

papers.title: Direct Topology Tracking in Continuous Implicit Models
papers.abstract: We present a framework for tracking topological features directly within continuous implicit models. Such models, including implicit neural representations (INRs) and multivariate functional approximations (MFAs), are increasingly adopted to represent scientific data without the resolution constraints of discrete grids. They offer compact, smooth, and differentiable representations of complex fields, enabling new opportunities for high-performance data storage, reconstruction, and analysis. Given a continuous implicit model, our method tracks the evolution of critical points by querying the model and its derivatives, thereby eliminating the need to resample onto a grid. This approach enables faithful feature tracking while avoiding discretization-induced artifacts such as aliasing. We demonstrate the generality of our framework across a range of implicit representations, including analytic functions, MFAs, and INRs, and show that it produces smooth, coherent critical point trajectories. By enabling feature tracking directly on continuous representations, our method supports a new class of feature-driven visualization workflows centered on implicit models.
